content: 1. Pexidartinib: This drug is metabolized by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is unavoidable, the dose of pexidartinib should be reduced as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the original pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 2. Clarithromycin and Phenindione: Clarithromycin increases the effects of phenindione by reducing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 3. Phenobarbital and Omeprazole: Phenobarbital decreases the levels and effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Clarithromycin and Pimavanserin: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Clarithromycin and Pirtobrutinib: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. After discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the original pirtobrutinib dose. 6. Clarithromycin and Pitolisant: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and clarithromycin increases pitolisant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Clarithromycin and Pomalidomide: Clarithromycin increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transport. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Clarithromycin and Ponatinib: Clarithromycin increases ponatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the starting dose of ponatinib to 30 mg daily. 9. Clarithromycin and Ponesimod: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 10. Clarithromycin and Pralsetinib: Clarithromycin increases pralsetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Clarithromycin and Prednisone: Clarithromycin increases prednisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Clarithromycin and Primaquine: Clarithromycin increases primaquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Clarithromycin and Procainamide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Clarithromycin and Prochlorperazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 15. Clarithromycin and Progesterone (Intravaginal Gel, Micronized, or Natural): Clarithromycin increases progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Clarithromycin and Promazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 17. Clarithromycin and Promethazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Clarithromycin and Propafenone: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 19. Clarithromycin and Protamines: Clarithromycin increases the effects of protamines by reducing their metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Clarithromycin and Protriptyline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 21. Clarithromycin and Quetiapine: Clarithromycin increases quetiapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 22. Clarithromycin and Quinidine: Clarithromycin increases quinidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 23. Quinupristin/Dalfopristin and Clarithromycin: This combination increases clarithromycin levels by reducing its metabolism. This is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. 24. Clarithromycin and Ranolazine: Clarithromycin increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 25. Clarithromycin and Repaglinide: Clarithromycin increases repaglinide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Clarithromycin and Repotrectinib: Clarithromycin increases repotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transport. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 27. Clarithromycin and Resmetirom: Clarithromycin increases resmetirom levels. Avoid co-administration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 28. Clarithromycin and Ribociclib: Clarithromycin increases ribociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Clarithromycin and Rifabutin: Clarithromycin increases rifabutin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 30. Rifampin and Omeprazole: Rifampin decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 31. Clarithromycin and Rimegepant: Clarithromycin increases rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transport. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 32. Clarithromycin and Rivaroxaban: Clarithromycin increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination in patients with impaired renal function. 33. Clarithromycin and Romidepsin: Clarithromycin increases romidepsin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 34. Clarithromycin and Rosuvastatin: Clarithromycin increases rosuvastatin toxicity. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 35. Clarithromycin and Ruxolitinib: Clarithromycin increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 36. Omeprazole and Secretin: Proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during secretin stimulation testing, falsely suggesting gastrinoma. Temporarily stop omeprazole at least 14 days before testing. 37. Clarithromycin and Selpercatinib: Clarithromycin increases selpercatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 38. Clarithromycin and Selumetinib: Clarithromycin increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the selumetinib dose if co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable. 39. Clarithromycin and Sertraline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 40. Clarithromycin and Sevoflurane: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 41. Clarithromycin and Sildenafil: Clarithromycin increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 42. Clarithromycin and Silodosin: Clarithromycin increases silodosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 43. Clarithromycin and Siponimod: Clarithromycin increases siponimod levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 44. Clarithromycin and Sirolimus: Clarithromycin increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 45. Omeprazole and Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Omeprazole decreases velpatasvir solubility by increasing gastric pH, reducing its effectiveness. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 46. Clarithromycin and Solifenacin: Clarithromycin increases solifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 47. Clarithromycin and Sonidegib: Clarithromycin increases sonidegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 48. Clarithromycin and Sorafenib: Clarithromycin increases sorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 49. Clarithromycin and Sotalol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 50. Omeprazole and Sotorasib: Omeprazole decreases sotorasib levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 51. Clarithromycin and Sparsentan: Clarithromycin increases sparsentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or interrupt sparsentan treatment if unavoidable. 52. Clarithromycin and Stiripentol: Clarithromycin increases stiripentol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 53. Tucatinib and Omeprazole: Tucatinib increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates. 54. Clarithromycin and Abemaciclib: Clarithromycin increases abemaciclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 55. Omeprazole and Abrocitinib: Omeprazole increases abrocitinib levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Start abrocitinib at 50 mg daily when co-administered with CYP2C19 inhibitors. 56. Clarithromycin and Albuterol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Clarithromycin and Alfentanil: Clarithromycin increases alfentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Clarithromycin and Alfuzosin: Clarithromycin increases alfuzosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Clarithromycin and Alosetron: Clarithromycin increases alosetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Clarithromycin and Amikacin: Clarithromycin increases amikacin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transport. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Clarithromycin and Amitriptyline: Clarithromycin increases amitriptyline levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transport. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Clarithromycin and Amlodipine: Clarithromycin increases amlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased effects of calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension, edema, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Amobarbital and Omeprazole: Amobarbital decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Omeprazole and Amphetamine: Reduced gastric acidity caused by proton pump inhibitors decreases the time to Tmax for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine. Use caution and monitor closely.
